item.content:encoded:
Agree with the SCP tailoring it's aggressive state to the viewer being over-the-top.
Also, vomiting that quickly is unlikely. Extreme distaste, unwillingness to recall events, etc is fine. But vomiting that quickly, no. Prolonged exposure, sure, with some viewers reacting sooner than others (obviously not everyone has a weak stomach, but very few people have cast iron stomachs), but not ten to fifteen seconds. I'm sure some people could withstand up to a hundred and twenty seconds, even if the images are as graphic as described.

As far as the camera, while it's true color photography existed then, it was likely unreliable, and there would be some difficulty in locating a color camera from that era; it would be easier to find a black and white one like mentioned. Would recomend changing to "A photograph of SCP-147 in its optimal state. A black-and-white camera had to be used to take this photo, due to difficulty locating a color camera that would not trigger a hostile state".
